_about.what: Gym — lower body — one move per object in "moves". The app reads this file directly: save it, reload the page. Every field name is checked, so a typo is reported with the file and move it is in.
_about.add: Copy a move that looks like the new one, paste it into "moves", give it a new id and change every field. Or: node scripts/catalog.js new <file> <id>  — writes a template with placeholder text to replace.
_about.remove: Delete the move's object (and the comma before or after it). Routines built in the app that used it will show it as missing.
_about.check: node scripts/catalog.js check  — or reload the app: a bad file shows the error on screen instead of the exercise list.
_about.names: Anything written as a word instead of an object — "metric": "knee", "template": "lean", "preset": "standing", "conditions": "balance" — is looked up in shared.json. Add reusable pieces there, not here.
_about.notes: Any field starting with "_" is a note for people and is ignored: "_note": "physio wants this re-checked".

fields.id: Unique name, used in links and saved sessions — never change it once the move has been used. Lower-case letters, digits, underscores. Good: "seated_knee_ext". Bad: "Seated Knee Ext", "knee-ext", "1_knee".
fields.name: What the user sees in the list. Good: "Seated knee extension". Bad: a clinical term nobody outside physio uses ("Open-chain terminal extension").
fields.clinicalName: Optional. The term a physio would use, shown in the details panel under the name.
fields.type: "reps" (counted) or "hold" (seconds in position). A stretch held for 30 s is a hold; ten slow raises are reps.
fields.view: "side" or "front" — where the phone stands. Side-on for anything that bends forward/back (knees, hips, spine); front-on for anything that goes out to the side (leg raise to the side, arm raise to the side, knees caving in).
fields.tracking: What the camera can honestly do: "form" (counts AND judges — needs at least one fault with a measurement and a threshold), "reps" (counts only; faults are listed for the person to watch), "none" (nothing to measure — the guide is shown and the set is logged by hand). Bad: "form" on a move whose faults are all words; the file will not load.
fields.vetted: Optional, true/false. true = a physio has recorded and checked this move in the Studio; vetted moves list first.
fields.equipment: List of words: ["none"], ["chair"], ["band", "door anchor"]. Optional extras say so: "ankle weight (optional)".
fields.muscles: { "primary": [...], "secondary": [...] } — plain names ("quadriceps", "gluteus medius"). primary must have at least one.
fields.sided: Only for one-sided moves: { "limb": "leg" | "arm" | "side", "by": "camera" | "pick", "auto": true }. "camera" = the limb nearest the phone is the working one (side-on moves); "pick" = the person chooses (front-on moves); "auto": true = when no side was chosen, watch both and follow the one that moves. Leave the field out for two-sided moves.
fields.upperBody: true when the legs need not be in frame (seated desk moves, shoulder work). Default false.
fields.summary: One line for the list. Good: "Sitting, straighten one knee until the leg is level, hold, and lower." Bad: a paragraph.
fields.setup: Where the phone goes and how to start, in the user's words. Good: "Sit tall on a chair, side-on to the phone, working leg nearest…" Bad: "Standard set-up."
fields.brief: What the coach SAYS out loud as the set begins: the position and the movement in one or two short sentences, no camera talk (the person has already placed the phone). Keep it under about 35 words — it is spoken while they get into position. Good: "Lie on your back, working leg straight. Slide the heel toward your bottom as far as it will go, then slide it back out." Bad: "Stand 2.5 m from the camera at hip height" (set-up, not movement) or a paragraph. Leave it out and the coach says only the name and the target.
fields.why: Why this camera angle can measure this move. Shown to the user; keeps the author honest. Good: "Side-on the knee angle runs from 90° to straight." Bad: left empty.
fields.calibrationPose: Optional. The still position held for the first two seconds of every set, which the coach measures against. Good: "Sitting tall, knee bent to 90°, foot hanging."
fields.camera: { "height": "floor" | "knee" | "hip" | "chest" | "eye", "distance": "2 m", "posture": "standing" | "sitting" | "lying" | "prone" | "sidelying" | "kneeling", "tolerance": 25 }. Leave it out to use the file's default at the top. posture also decides how the stick figure is pinned in place, and how a crooked phone is levelled at calibration (a standing or sitting trunk is upright, a lying one is along the floor; kneeling makes no assumption). tolerance: degrees the person may turn away from the ideal view mid-set before the coach says to turn back; leave it out for the settings.json default. Good: 20–30. Bad: 5 (nobody stands that still) or 60 (the joint is hidden by then).
fields.targets: Optional list of rep counts / hold seconds the bubble cycles through, e.g. [6, 8, 10, 12]. Leave it out for the standard choices in settings.json.
fields.defaultTarget: The one of targets selected to begin with. Must be in the list. Leave it out with targets.
fields.progress: How far through a rep the person is. { "metric": <measurement>, "start": "calibrated" | number, "target": number | "opt:rom" }. "calibrated" = whatever the measurement reads in the start position; "startMin"/"startMax" clamp it (a knee that calibrates at 150° is treated as 160°). target = the reading at a full rep, or with "targetIsDelta": true a change from the start — "delta": -1 when the reading goes DOWN during the rep (a knee angle closing). Only for type "reps" with tracking "form" or "reps". Good: knee angle from calibrated to 172. Bad: start and target the same number.
fields.show: What the coach asks the person to demonstrate once, before the set, so the target is measured on their body instead of assumed: { "ask": "arms straight out to the sides, level with your shoulders, nothing in your hands" }. They hold that pose still for a moment, with the band or weight out of the way, and what it reads becomes progress.target for the set. Only for a counted move, and only worth it when the number in progress.target depends on the body or the angle — a raise to shoulder height, a hands-apart distance — or when the equipment hides the joints. progress.target is still required: it is the fallback, and the sanity check (a demonstration under 40% or over 250% of it is refused). Good: one short sentence naming the end position. Bad: "do the exercise".
fields.hold: For type "hold" with tracking on: { "conditions": [ { "metric": <measurement>, "rel": "abs" | "change", "min": n, "max": n } ] } — the hold counts while every condition is met. "change" = relative to the calibrated start. A condition may carry "when": [{ "option": "variant", "is": "bent" }] so it only applies for that option. A named set ("balance") comes from shared.json.
fields.display: Optional. What the live readout shows: { "label": "bend", "unit": "°", "from": "start" } shows the progress measurement as a change from the start ("abs" = the raw reading); for a hold, { "condition": 0, "label": "knee", "aim": "90°" } shows that hold condition. Without it the app shows the raw progress reading.
fields.enterCue: Optional, holds only: what the coach says when the person has been out of position for a few seconds. Good: "Slide down the wall until your knees are at ninety".
fields.faults: What goes wrong, in the order they matter. Each: { "id", "label", "cue" (spoken, ≤ 8 words, what TO do), "tip" (written, why it matters), "severity" 1–3 }. Add "metric", "op" ("<" or ">"), "threshold" and the camera watches for it; leave those out and it is listed for the person to watch. "minP" (0–1) = ignore until this far into the rep; "persist" ms before it is spoken, "cooldown" ms before the same cue may repeat (rules included, so one that is true every rep is not said every rep); "rel": "change" compares to the calibrated start. "when": a list of gates that must all hold for the fault to count — { "option": "variant", "is": "bent" }, { "metric": <measurement>, "op": "<", "threshold": 168 }, "inPosition" or "notInPosition". "phase": "moving" / "rest" (reps) or "any" (a hold fault that must fire while the person is OUT of position; otherwise hold faults only watch the held position). "scale": { "metric": "progress", "times": 0.35 } makes the threshold grow with another reading. Rules instead of a measurement: "rule": "shallow" (rep did not reach the target), "fast" with "minMs", "return" with "threshold" (rep ended above this progress — did not come all the way back). Or "template": "lean" with a "threshold" to reuse one from shared.json. Good cue: "Sit tall". Bad cue: "You are leaning back again" (tells them what is wrong, not what to do).
fields.guide: { "surface": what to stand/lie on, "stop": when to stop, "cannotSee": what the person must check themselves, "regions": [ { "name": "Trunk", "points": [ { "t": "one form point", "tracked": true|false } ] } ] }. tracked: true only when a fault with a measurement actually checks that point — it is shown to the user as "camera watches".
fields.pose: The two-frame stick figure. { "A": start keyframe, "B": end keyframe, "work": { "thigh": 1, "glute": 0.5 } muscles to light up 0–1, "props": [ { "kind": "box" | "bar" | "disc" | "band", "at": "hip" } ], "wall": "behind" | "ahead", "anchor": joint(s) that stay put }. Side-view keyframe angles in degrees: torso (from vertical, + = leaning forward), thigh & shin (from hanging straight down, + = forward), foot (+ = toes up), uarm & farm (arms, + = forward), plus the far limb: thighF, shinF, footF, uarmF, farmF; face: "right" | "left". Front-view: legL, legR, shinL, shinR, armL, armR, foreL, foreR (+ = out to the side), lean, headTilt, squat 0–1. "preset": "standing" | "seated" | "supine" | "prone" | "quadruped" fills the usual values first. Check it on /figures.html.
fields.tempo: Free text. Good: "Up 2 s, hold 2 s, down 3 s."
fields.contraindications: When not to do it. Shown as "Do not do this if".
fields.sources: Optional list of { "name", "url" } added to the file's own sources.
fields.band: Optional. "none", "yellow", "red"… = offers the band-colour bubble with that default; true = offers it defaulting to none.
fields.minMs: Optional, reps only: the quickest a rep may take before "Too fast" fires (when the move lists no live fault of its own). Default in settings.json.
fields.options: Advanced: extra bubbles, e.g. a range target { "key": "rom", "label": "Range target", "values": [45, 60, 75, 90], "unit": "°", "default": 90 } referenced from progress.target as "opt:rom".
fields.figure: Advanced: point keyframes captured by the Studio instead of pose angles. Prefer pose.
fields.focus: Advanced: the landmark the live view highlights, e.g. "KNEE". Default: the last point of the progress measurement.
fields.group: Optional. The heading the move is listed under; default = the file's group at the top.
fields.region: Optional. The body region for filtering; default = the file's region.
fields.icon: Optional short label used where an icon is expected. Default "move".
fields.order: Optional. Position in the list; default = the file's order + position in this file.

moves.name: Bodyweight squat
moves.summary: Feet shoulder-width, sit the hips down and back until the thighs are about level, then stand.
moves.setup: Face the phone, feet shoulder-width, toes a little out, arms in front. Sit down and back until the thighs are near parallel, knees tracking over the toes, then drive up to standing.
moves.brief: Feet shoulder-width, toes a little out, arms in front. Sit down and back until the thighs are near parallel, knees tracking over the toes, then drive up to standing.
moves.why: Facing the phone both knees are seen: depth from the knee angle, and the knees caving toward each other as the gap between them shrinking.
moves.progression: Goblet squat; slower lowering; pause at the bottom.
moves.contraindications: Knee pain at depth; unable to keep the heels down.

faults.label: Not reaching the target
faults.tip: Take each rep through the full range you set — half reps count as partials.

faults.label: Too fast
faults.tip: Control both directions; momentum takes the work away from the muscle.

faults.label: Heels lifting
faults.tip: Sit back into the hips; if the heels lift, raise them on a small plate for now.

faults.label: Tailbone tucking under
faults.tip: At the bottom the pelvis can tuck and round the lower back. Your depth ends just before that.

faults.label: Cutting depth
faults.tip: Go as deep as the heels stay down and the back stays neutral.

faults.label: Looking up
faults.tip: Craning up extends the neck. Look at a spot on the floor a few metres away.

guide.surface: Flat floor, flat shoes or bare feet.
guide.cannotSee: The back rounding and the hips travelling back — side-view details.

points.t: Track over the toes; stay apart at the bottom.

moves.name: Goblet squat
moves.summary: Holding a weight at the chest, squat deep with the elbows inside the knees and the chest up.
moves.setup: Stand side-on to the phone, a dumbbell held vertically at the chest. Sit down between the heels until the thighs are at or below parallel, keeping the chest up, then stand.
moves.brief: Stand with a dumbbell held vertically at the chest. Sit down between the heels until the thighs are at or below parallel, chest up, then stand.
moves.why: From the side the knee angle gives depth and the shoulder–hip line shows the trunk folding forward, which the weight at the chest tends to prevent.
moves.contraindications: Knee pain at depth; lower back pain with the weight.

faults.label: Not reaching the target
faults.tip: Take each rep through the full range you set — half reps count as partials.

faults.label: Too fast
faults.tip: Control both directions; momentum takes the work away from the muscle.

faults.label: Heels lifting
faults.tip: Spread the floor with the feet; heels stay planted.

faults.label: Lower back rounding at the bottom
faults.tip: Squat only as deep as the lower back stays neutral.

faults.label: Weight drifting away from the chest
faults.tip: The weight rests against the chest. Letting it drift out pulls you forward.

guide.cannotSee: The knees caving — a front-view detail.

points.t: Chest up; weight tight to the body.

moves.name: Sumo squat
moves.summary: Wide stance, toes turned out, sit straight down with the knees following the toes.
moves.setup: Face the phone with the feet wide and toes turned out about 45°. Sit straight down, knees pushing out over the toes, until the thighs are near level, then stand.
moves.brief: Stand with the feet wide and toes turned out about 45 degrees. Sit straight down, knees pushing out over the toes, until the thighs are near level, then stand.
moves.why: Facing the phone the knee angle gives depth and the knees drifting inward — the main fault in a wide stance — is measured as the gap between them shrinking.
moves.progression: Hold a dumbbell between the legs.
moves.contraindications: Groin strain; hip pinching at depth.

faults.label: Not reaching the target
faults.tip: Take each rep through the full range you set — half reps count as partials.

faults.label: Too fast
faults.tip: Control both directions; momentum takes the work away from the muscle.

faults.label: Trunk tipping forward
faults.cue: Chest up, sit between the heels
faults.tip: A sumo squat is more upright than a normal squat; sit down, not back.

faults.label: Knees not tracking the toes
faults.tip: In a wide stance the knees must travel out over the toes, not forward.

faults.label: Bouncing at the bottom
faults.tip: Bouncing out of the bottom loads the groin. Pause and push.

guide.cannotSee: The trunk tipping forward — a side-view detail.

points.t: Follow the toes outward all the way down.
Upright; weight hangs between the legs.

moves.name: Forward lunge
moves.summary: Step forward and lower until both knees are at about 90°, then push back to standing.
moves.setup: Stand side-on to the phone, working leg nearest. Step that foot forward and lower straight down until the front thigh is level and the back knee hovers above the floor. Push off the front foot to return.
moves.brief: Stand tall. Step the working foot forward and lower straight down until the front thigh is level and the back knee hovers above the floor.
moves.why: From the side the front knee angle gives depth, and the trunk pitching forward — the usual cheat — shows as the shoulder–hip line tilting.
moves.regression: Split squat with no step; shorter step.
moves.contraindications: Kneecap pain on the front leg; balance problems.

faults.label: Not reaching the target
faults.tip: Take each rep through the full range you set — half reps count as partials.

faults.label: Too fast
faults.tip: Control both directions; momentum takes the work away from the muscle.

faults.label: Knee dropping inward
faults.tip: The front knee tracks over the foot. Inward collapse is the commonest lunge fault.

faults.label: Front knee shooting past the toes
faults.tip: Take a longer step so the shin stays close to upright; the knee should stay over the foot.

faults.label: Step too short
faults.tip: A short step drives the knee far past the toes and loads the kneecap.

faults.label: Not lowering enough
faults.tip: Drop the back knee toward the floor; the front thigh should reach level.

faults.label: Front heel lifting
faults.tip: Drive up through the front heel; if it lifts, the stride is too short or the weight is on the toes.

guide.surface: Enough floor for a long step.

points.t: Thigh reaches level; shin near vertical.

moves.name: Reverse lunge
moves.summary: Step back and lower until the back knee nearly touches, then drive up through the front heel.
moves.setup: Stand side-on to the phone, working (front) leg nearest. Step the other foot back and lower until the front thigh is level, then push through the front heel to stand.
moves.brief: Stand tall. Step the other foot back and lower until the front thigh is level, then push through the front heel to stand.
moves.why: From the side the front knee angle closes every rep, so reps are counted. The trunk lean is smaller than in a forward lunge and is listed rather than judged.
moves.progression: Dumbbells; deficit from a low step.
moves.contraindications: Kneecap pain on the front leg.

faults.label: Not reaching the target
faults.tip: Take each rep through the full range you set — half reps count as partials.

faults.label: Too fast
faults.tip: Control both directions; momentum takes the work away from the muscle.

faults.label: Trunk tipping forward
faults.tip: Lower straight down; the back knee travels to the floor, the chest stays up.

faults.label: Pushing off the back foot
faults.tip: The back foot is a kickstand; the front leg does the work.

faults.label: Front heel lifting
faults.tip: Weight through the front heel is what puts the work in the glute.

faults.label: Folding forward
faults.tip: A little forward lean is fine; folding shifts the load to the lower back.

guide.cannotSee: Which leg is doing the pushing.

points.t: Thigh reaches level; heel stays down.

moves.name: Walking lunge
moves.summary: Lunge forward and, instead of stepping back, bring the rear foot through into the next lunge.
moves.setup: Start at one end of the room. Lunge forward, then step the back foot through into the next lunge. Keep going for the distance.
moves.why: Walking takes you out of frame within a few steps. Logged by hand.

faults.label: Knee dropping inward
faults.tip: Momentum makes inward collapse more likely here than in a static lunge.

faults.label: Trunk tipping forward
faults.tip: Lower straight down each step.

faults.label: Walking a tightrope
faults.tip: Land with the feet hip-width apart, not in one line, or balance eats the set.

faults.label: Wobbling side to side
faults.tip: Keep the feet hip-width apart, not on a tightrope.

guide.cannotSee: You — the exercise walks out of frame.

moves.name: Lateral lunge
moves.summary: Step wide to one side and sit into that hip, the other leg straight, then push back.
moves.setup: Face the phone, feet together. Step wide to the working side and sit the hips back over that foot, the other leg straight, then push back to the start.
moves.brief: Feet together. Step wide to the working side and sit the hips back over that foot, the other leg straight, then push back to the start.
moves.why: Facing the phone the knees move far apart on every step, so reps are counted; where the weight sits is listed rather than judged.
moves.progression: Hold a dumbbell at the chest.
moves.contraindications: Groin strain; knee pain on the bent side.

faults.label: Not reaching the target
faults.tip: Take each rep through the full range you set — half reps count as partials.

faults.label: Too fast
faults.tip: Control both directions; momentum takes the work away from the muscle.

faults.label: Bent knee caving inward
faults.tip: Sit back into the hip so the knee stays over the middle of the foot.

faults.label: Toes turning out
faults.tip: Turning the stepping foot out moves the work from the groin to the front of the hip.

faults.label: Toes turning out
faults.tip: Both feet point at the phone; the stretch is in the straight leg's inner thigh.

faults.label: Bending the trailing knee
faults.tip: The leg you are not sitting into stays straight; that is where the stretch belongs.

points.t: Knee over the foot; hips sit back.
Feet wide apart at the bottom.

moves.name: Romanian deadlift
moves.summary: Weights in hand, hinge at the hips with soft knees until the hamstrings pull, then stand tall.
moves.setup: Stand side-on to the phone, weights in front of the thighs, knees soft. Push the hips back and let the weights slide down the legs, back flat, until the hamstrings pull. Drive the hips forward to stand.
moves.brief: Stand with the weights in front of the thighs, knees soft. Push the hips back and let the weights slide down the legs, back flat, until the hamstrings pull.
moves.why: From the side the shoulder–hip line hinges toward horizontal each rep, and the knees bending to turn it into a squat is caught by the knee angle.
moves.regression: Bodyweight hip hinge with a dowel on the back.

faults.label: Not reaching the target
faults.tip: Take each rep through the full range you set — half reps count as partials.

faults.label: Too fast
faults.tip: Control both directions; momentum takes the work away from the muscle.

faults.label: Back rounding
faults.tip: Stop the descent when the back starts to round; chest proud, chin neutral.

faults.label: Weight drifting away from the legs
faults.tip: The weight stays in contact with the legs. Away from the body it becomes a back exercise.

faults.label: Weights drifting away from the legs
faults.tip: Drag the weights down the thighs; away from the body loads the lower back.

faults.label: Squatting instead of hinging
faults.tip: Knees stay softly bent and still. The hips travel backwards.

faults.label: Snapping the hips at the top
faults.cue: Stand tall, do not lean back
faults.tip: Finishing by leaning back hyperextends the lower back. Stop at upright.

guide.cannotSee: The back rounding under a shirt.

points.t: Travel back; trunk hinges toward level.

moves.name: Single-leg Romanian deadlift
moves.summary: Balancing on one leg, hinge forward as the other leg lifts behind, then return.
moves.setup: Stand side-on to the phone on the working leg, knee soft. Hinge at the hip, reaching the free leg straight back and the hands toward the floor, until the body is near level. Return to standing.
moves.brief: Stand on the working leg, knee soft. Hinge at the hip, reaching the free leg straight back and the hands toward the floor, until the body is near level.
moves.why: From the side the trunk hinges toward horizontal every rep, so reps are counted. Hip rotation — the main fault — is a front-view detail.
moves.progression: Hold a weight; slow the lowering.
moves.regression: Fingertips on a wall; smaller hinge.
moves.contraindications: Balance problems without support; hamstring strain.

faults.label: Not reaching the target
faults.tip: Take each rep through the full range you set — half reps count as partials.

faults.label: Too fast
faults.tip: Control both directions; momentum takes the work away from the muscle.

faults.label: Hip opening to the side
faults.tip: Point the free toes at the floor so the pelvis stays level.

faults.label: Back rounding
faults.tip: Reach the head forward and the heel back; stop before the back rounds.

faults.label: Rushing to stay balanced
faults.tip: Speed hides poor balance. Three seconds down is the standard.

guide.surface: Flat floor; a wall in reach.

points.t: Reaches back in line with the trunk; toes down.

moves.name: Dumbbell deadlift
moves.summary: Weights on the floor beside the feet; hinge and bend to grip them, then stand tall by driving the floor away.
moves.setup: Stand side-on to the phone, weights beside the feet. Push the hips back and bend the knees to reach the weights with a flat back, then stand by driving the legs and hips together. Lower the same way.
moves.brief: Stand with the weights beside the feet. Push the hips back and bend the knees to reach them with a flat back, then stand by driving the legs and hips together.
moves.why: From the side the trunk hinges and returns each rep, and the back folding further than the hips — the sign of a rounded pull — shows as the trunk angle dropping too far.
moves.regression: Weights on a low step; kettlebell between the feet.
moves.contraindications: Lower back pain; unable to keep a flat back at the bottom.

faults.label: Not reaching the target
faults.tip: Take each rep through the full range you set — half reps count as partials.

faults.label: Too fast
faults.tip: Control both directions; momentum takes the work away from the muscle.

faults.label: Back rounding
faults.tip: Brace, chest proud, and lift the weights from a higher surface if the back rounds.

faults.label: Rounding at the bottom
faults.tip: If the back rounds to reach the floor, start from a raised surface instead.

faults.label: Hips shooting up first
faults.tip: The shoulders and hips rise at the same rate; if the hips lead, the back finishes the lift.

faults.label: Jerking off the floor
faults.tip: Pull the tension on first, then stand. A jerk loads the back before it is braced.

guide.cannotSee: The back rounding under a shirt.

points.t: Hinges with a flat back; stands fully tall.
Knees bend enough to reach the weights; heels down.

moves.name: Good morning
moves.summary: Hands behind the head, hinge at the hips with a flat back until the trunk is near level, then stand.
moves.setup: Stand side-on to the phone, hands behind the head, knees soft. Push the hips back and bow forward with a flat back until the trunk is near level, then squeeze the glutes to stand.
moves.brief: Stand with the hands behind the head, knees soft. Push the hips back and bow forward with a flat back until the trunk is near level, then squeeze the glutes to stand.
moves.why: From the side the trunk angle gives the hinge, and the knees bending to cheat is caught by the knee angle.
moves.progression: Band around the neck and under the feet; light bar.

faults.label: Not reaching the target
faults.tip: Take each rep through the full range you set — half reps count as partials.

faults.label: Too fast
faults.tip: Control both directions; momentum takes the work away from the muscle.

faults.label: Back rounding
faults.tip: Stop before the back rounds; the range grows as the hamstrings loosen.

faults.label: Going too low
faults.tip: Your depth ends where the back would round, usually well above horizontal.

faults.label: Looking up
faults.tip: Craning to look forward as you fold hyperextends the neck.

moves.name: Bulgarian split squat
moves.summary: Rear foot on a bench behind you, lower the front thigh to level and drive back up.
moves.setup: Stand a long step in front of a bench, side-on to the phone, working leg nearest and the other foot resting on the bench. Lower straight down until the front thigh is level, then push back up.
moves.brief: Stand a long step in front of a bench with the other foot resting on it. Lower straight down until the front thigh is level, then push back up.
moves.why: From the side the front knee angle closes and opens each rep, so reps are counted.
moves.regression: Split squat with the back foot on the floor.

faults.label: Not reaching the target
faults.tip: Take each rep through the full range you set — half reps count as partials.

faults.label: Too fast
faults.tip: Control both directions; momentum takes the work away from the muscle.

faults.label: Front knee caving inward
faults.tip: Push the knee out over the little toe.

faults.label: Trunk folding forward
faults.tip: A slight forward lean is fine; folding shifts the work to the back.

faults.label: Rear foot too high
faults.tip: A high rear foot arches the lower back. Knee height or lower is plenty.

faults.label: Stance too short
faults.tip: Too close and the front knee is driven far over the toes.

guide.surface: A stable bench that will not slide.

moves.name: Curtsy lunge
moves.summary: Step one leg diagonally behind the other and lower, as if curtsying, then return.
moves.setup: Face the phone. Step the free leg back and across behind the standing leg, lower until the front thigh is near level, then push back up.
moves.why: The legs cross in front of each other from the front and the step goes away from a side phone. Logged by hand.
moves.regression: Shorter step; hand on a support.

faults.label: Front knee caving
faults.tip: The front knee stays over the front foot even as the other leg crosses behind.

faults.label: Hips turning
faults.tip: Only the leg crosses; the pelvis keeps facing forward.

faults.label: Twisting the hips
faults.tip: Let the legs cross without the pelvis turning, or the knee takes the twist.

faults.label: Too deep too soon
faults.tip: This is a harder position for the knee than a normal lunge. Earn the depth.

moves.name: Glute kickback (quadruped)
moves.summary: On hands and knees, drive one heel up and back until the thigh is level with the back, then lower.
moves.setup: Hands under the shoulders, knees under the hips, side-on to the phone at knee height, working leg nearest. Keeping the knee bent, push the heel toward the ceiling until the thigh is in line with the back. Lower without resting the knee.
moves.brief: Hands under the shoulders, knees under the hips. Keeping the knee bent, push the working heel toward the ceiling until the thigh is in line with the back.
moves.why: From the side the working thigh swings from hanging to level each rep, so reps are counted. The back arching to lift higher is listed, not judged.
moves.tempo: Up 1 s, squeeze 1 s, down 2 s.
moves.progression: Band around the foot; ankle weight.
moves.contraindications: Lower back pain on the lift; wrist pain.

faults.label: Not reaching the target
faults.tip: Take each rep through the full range you set — half reps count as partials.

faults.label: Too fast
faults.tip: Control both directions; momentum takes the work away from the muscle.

faults.label: Arching the lower back
faults.tip: Most of a big kickback is lower-back arch, not hip. Lift only to the line of the body.

faults.label: Lower back arching
faults.tip: Higher than the back means the spine is lifting, not the glute.

faults.label: Weight shifting to one side
faults.tip: Keep the weight even over both hands and the resting knee.

faults.label: Head lifting
faults.tip: The head stays in line with the spine, not looking forward.

points.t: Thigh lifts to level with the back; knee bent.

moves.name: Jump squat
moves.summary: Squat down and jump up, landing softly back into the squat.
moves.setup: Face the phone, feet shoulder-width. Squat to about a quarter depth, jump as high as you can, and land quietly with the knees bending to absorb it.
moves.brief: Stand with the feet shoulder-width. Squat to about a quarter depth, jump as high as you can, and land quietly with the knees bending to absorb it.
moves.why: Facing the phone the knee angle dips before each jump, so reps are counted. Landing mechanics happen too fast to judge reliably.
moves.regression: Small hops; squat with a heel raise.
moves.contraindications: Knee or ankle injury; anyone told to avoid impact.

faults.label: Not reaching the target
faults.tip: Take each rep through the full range you set — half reps count as partials.

faults.label: Too fast
faults.tip: Control both directions; momentum takes the work away from the muscle.

faults.label: Landing with stiff legs
faults.tip: Bend the knees and hips on landing so it is quiet.

faults.label: Knees caving on landing
faults.tip: Land with the knees over the toes.

faults.label: Landing stiff and loud
faults.tip: Noise is force. Absorb the landing through the hips and knees.

faults.label: Knees caving on landing
faults.tip: The landing is where knees collapse inward. Stop the set when they do.

guide.surface: A floor with some give; not concrete.

points.t: Dip into a quarter squat before every jump.
Bend on the landing; track over the toes.

moves.name: Box jump
moves.summary: Jump onto a box with both feet and land softly in a quarter squat; step down.
moves.setup: Stand a short distance from a stable box. Swing the arms, jump and land with the whole foot on the box, knees soft. Stand tall, then step down.
moves.why: The person changes height and position between the floor and the box, which confuses the calibrated counter. Logged by hand.
moves.contraindications: Knee, ankle or Achilles injury; anyone told to avoid impact.

faults.label: Jumping back down
faults.tip: Jumping down is where box-jump injuries happen and it adds nothing.

faults.label: Landing in a deep squat
faults.tip: A deep landing means the box is too high; the hips should land above the knees.

faults.label: Jumping down
faults.tip: The jump down loads the tendons more than the jump up. Step.

faults.label: Tucking the knees to reach
faults.tip: If you have to tuck to land, the box is too high. You should finish standing straight.

points.t: Whole foot on the box; knees soft; hips above the knees.
